title: Label a node

samples.expr: let two = { id = 0; op = "2"; src = [] } in let three = { id = 1; op = "3"; src = [] } in label { id = 2; op = "add"; src = [two; three] }
samples.label: let two = { id = 0; op = "2"; src = [] } in let three = { id = 1; op = "3"; src = [] } in label { id = 2; op = "add"; src = [two; three] }

hints: The starter already builds the id and the op. You only need to add one more piece of text on the end with `^`.
`List.length n.src` counts the sources. It is an int, so turn it into text with `string_of_int`.
Add `^ " (" ^ string_of_int (List.length n.src) ^ ")"` to the end of the line.

answer.explain: The reference reads all three fields with a dot: `string_of_int n.id ^ ": " ^ n.op ^ " (" ^ string_of_int (List.length n.src) ^ ")"`. `n.src` is an ordinary list, so every list function from O.3 works on it.
